instruction: Install the unpacked Chrome extension from /home/user/Desktop/. Verify the popup HTML contains the heading 'Hello Extensions'.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation:
This task verifies the popup HTML file contains the expected heading '

Hello Extensions

'. Verified from the original hello.html file content.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic mismatch: Instruction requires verifying the extension is INSTALLED in Chrome and the popup contains the heading, but the getter only reads the source HTML file from disk (/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension/hello.html)
No installation verification: The evaluator cannot detect if the extension was actually loaded into Chrome - it would pass even if installation failed as long as the source file exists
Wrong state extraction: The getter reads a static file rather than verifying Chrome's runtime extension state or popup content

Incomplete coverage: The instruction has two requirements (1. Install extension, 2. Verify popup HTML), but the evaluator only checks that the source file contains text - it doesn't verify installation happened
State accessibility issue: The getter doesn't interact with Chrome's extension system (e.g., via CDP, chrome://extensions, or popup interaction)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) to query installed extensions and verify the extension is loaded
Read the popup HTML from Chrome's extension directory (e.g., ~/.config/google-chrome/.../Extensions/) rather than the source directory
Add postconfig to open the extension popup and verify content via accessibility tree or screenshot
Use Chrome CDP to get extension info and read the actual popup.html from the installed extension
At minimum, verify the extension appears in chrome://extensions page using accessibility tree or Chrome API
